destination.name: Tenterfield
destination.tagline: A New England Highway town tied to Federation, with granite country to its north.
destination.description: Tenterfield is a town of 4,066 people (2016 census) at 850 m on the Northern Tablelands, where the New England and Bruxner highways meet. Sir Henry Parkes gave his 1889 Federation oration at its School of Arts, which is now a museum and theatre. North of town, Bald Rock is Australia's largest granite monolith and Boonoo Boonoo has a waterfall with rock pools.
whyVisit: Walk onto Bald Rock's granite dome
Visit the Sir Henry Parkes School of Arts

goodToKnow.title: Bring correct change
goodToKnow.detail: Bald Rock and Boonoo Boonoo charge $8 per vehicle per day, collected by self-registration, so carry the right change.

goodToKnow.title: Parks can close
goodToKnow.detail: Both parks are always open but may close for poor weather or fire danger.

goodToKnow.title: Visitor centre
goodToKnow.detail: The visitor centre at 157 Rouse Street is open Monday to Friday 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM, Saturday 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM and Sunday 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM (Wikivoyage, 2019).

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Come in {months}: Wikivoyage lists an Autumn Festival around Easter, and spring and autumn suit walking to Bald Rock and the falls.
